statement: Using de Moivre's theorem, express $\sin 5\theta$ as a polynomial in $\sin\theta$.
solution: $(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)^{5}=\cos 5\theta+i\sin 5\theta$. The imaginary part is $5\cos^{4}\theta\sin\theta-10\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{3}\theta+\sin^{5}\theta$. With $\cos^{2}\theta=1-\sin^{2}\theta$ this becomes $\sin\theta\bigl(5(1-s^{2})^{2}-10(1-s^{2})s^{2}+s^{4}\bigr)$ where $s=\sin\theta$, i.e. $\sin 5\theta=5\sin\theta-20\sin^{3}\theta+16\sin^{5}\theta$.
hints: Take the imaginary part and rewrite cosines in terms of sine.
